newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys recover late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys recover late.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended narrowly mixed after a late short covering rally ahead of Thursday's USDA export sales figures and Friday's USDA Supply and Demand Report, traders said.

"The way we closed yesterday brought in some follow-through technical selling and there were expectations tomorrow's export sales report would show rather paltry sale of soybeans, which is quite possible," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer.
He added that reports of additional crop losses in Argentina propelled the late short covering rally.
"We know the Argentine crop is below earlier promise," Lekberg added. "It's not exactly new news, it's just that it caught a lot of traders short."
Funds were aggressive sellers on the day, accounting for at least 18 million bushels in sales, pit sources said. They pointed to a weak technical close on Tuesday.
Soybeans closed 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-3/4 cents lower with May down 1-3/4 at $8.47-1/2.
Traders said sentiment on the floor was shifting from a bullish mood, tied to tight U.S. soybean stocks and strong world demand, to a bearish one.
They cited ideas USDA would not cut ending soybean stocks in Friday's USDA Supply and Demand Report and indications world buyers were increasingly relying on South American supplies.
Analysts expected soybean stocks to fall only slightly in Friday's supply/demand report and not as far as some floor sources had expected.
Soybeans rallied last week on ideas USDA would slash 22 million bushels off the already-tight ending stocks figure after last week's 22-million-bushel downward revision in quarterly stocks.

Weather was also deemed bearish for soybeans. Forecasts called for another week of cold, wet weather and traders speculated fields would remain too damp for corn plantings. Farmers may be forced to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans, some sources speculated.
The July/November closed at $1.50-1/2, premium July.

On the day, Cargill Inc sold four million bushels May and one million July, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer and Griffin Trading each sold four million July, Refco Inc sold two million May and four million July and Iowa Grain sold three million May and two million July, pit sources said.
Farmers Commodities Corp spread one million bushels November/July at $1.42 to $1.43, premium July.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 850 May $8.00 puts at 3-1/2 and bought 850 May $8.25 puts at 9-1/2 to 10-3/4 cents. Produce Grain sold 400 May $8.00 puts at three to 3-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, above Tuesday's actual volume of 59,935 contracts.
